questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Going with my friends in the south of Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great people, great adventures, great studies.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It needed time, but I would say it was quite easy. Sometimes you just need to let go of your worries, because it will all figure out when you arrive in Milan. Just remember the deadlines, of course.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome letter I think, but I do not remember that much assistance. It is a good idea to ally yourself with another Erasmus-student, but if not I am sure you will make it anyways. The first week we tried out different courses. It was a bit chaotic for my mind, but after the week I had set a really good schema for myself. Also the professors are helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Did it with three of my friends through HousingAnywhere, quite easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try to find something in an okay price early in the process. For me, it was nice to live a bit outside of the city (in Navigli area) and we payed 4.400DKK every month.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You will find and understand all these things when you arrive. The italian system is a lot different than the danish, but it is easy to align and adapt to when you arrive.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You registrate to exams before the course is ended. t

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Students and also the professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I changed 4/5 courses when I arrived, because some of them was not rolling in the first trimester, and also some of them I did not found interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it easy. <33

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is different than studying in copenhagen. Some times more noise. More italian. Different communication. Different expectations. But overall it was interesting to try out another system, even though I prefer the danish.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All of them were master courses, and even though I was on my bachelor I found the level quite good for me. Sometimes easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More lecture based than seminar style, witch I am more used to in Copenhagen. Sometimes the teachers have a very italian accent when speaking english, but it will be easier to understand as time passes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Narrating and negotiating identities (6ECTS)
The politics of displacement, mobility and asylum (9ECTS)
Political order, violence and institutions (9ECTS)
Workshop: Human trafficking/smuggling (3ECTS)
Laboratorio: Understanding the politics of care (3ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of my courses were really interesting and good !
Political order was very interesting, like political science / political philosophy and the professor is very proficient and capable (Juan Masullo). 
I am interested in global migration, therefore The politics of displacement, mobility and asylum, Workshop: Human trafficking/smuggling , and Narrating and negotiating identities (here the linguist, Paola, on the 2nd part of the course was so good) was truly inspiring and insightful for me. Laboratorio: Understanding the politics of care was also a nice friday-course and the teacher, Camille Allard, was very nice and a sociologist.

questions.answer:
A train ticket fine at Cinque Terre...
A vacuum cleaner...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in supermarket. Also, a glass of wine at good local spots is around 3euros. A good visit on the best local restaurants is no more than 20 euros (and then u get sooo good food, wine, desssert like tiramisu, TRY Brutto Anatroccolo and Trattorio Bolognese). The ATM-cart (local transport in the whole city of Milan) is only 22euros per month. The coffee, only 1-1,20euros for caffe macchiato.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Harder to find. Easier after you find italian friends who can show you around. Tried the boulder club, expensive as in cph. But there are sooo many good museums, bars, cafes, areas, when you get into the city and its vibration you can find cool places.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university was not that visible with social activities, witch was sad... There was something called ESN for international students, but I did not tried it out actually...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: GO AROUND IN ITALY. Take the train one-hour north to Como and Lecco lake and hike. Go to Napoli, Rome and Sicily. Easy and cheap with flix-bus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Italy has the sea, the mountain and a very beautiful land. Go around and explore, especially in the summer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy I would say. Italians like when you try to adapt to the culture, are curious about the food and their language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to approach them by yourself. People meet people when they see each other on the same wavelength as just another friend, we are not that different in the end. I got a good friend from Milan , she is the best, many of the same interests.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language definately! The young generation of course speaks good engish, but sometimes it was harder to communicate with elders.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The mindset. La Calma. Maden, menneskerne, varmen (om sommeren), sproget, sporvognene, larmen, generationernes forbundethed, æstetikken, kaffen, musikken.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Ro på, opsøg internationale eller italienske studerende (det er for fedt at møde folk fra andre lande!!) og vær nysgerrig <33

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ottica er et nice område. Den sicilienske restaurant 'Eolina' er nice. Hvis du vil studere i ro og fred tog jeg selv på 'Combo' og læste, men der er også mange hyggelige caféer i hele byen. NAPOLI pizza er så lækkertt og der ligger en god napolitansk restaurant ved Navigli-kanalen der hedder 'I Segreti di Pulcinella' (men prøv ogs lige San Michele i Napoli).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people <33

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sprogbarriere nogle gange (for mig ifbm at være på hospitalet)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Nyd det! Det er en oplevelse du bærer med dig hele livet<33

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
